headline: Committee discusses hotel-district rezoning for apartments with vacation rentals

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.summary: Members took up a limit on rezoning based on 2008 resident use; a version not applying to flood hazard areas passed. The chair said conditions will be set after Maui Planning Commission review. A motion to adopt a resolution was pending when the recording ended.
meeting.recap: The Housing and Land Use Committee reconvened its August 5 meeting on September 9, 2026.[[0:00:24]] Council Tamara Paltin proposed conditions such as public beach access and an updated state-certified shoreline assessment.[[0:38:59]] The chair said conditions would be set later, after the Maui Planning Commission reviews them.[[0:46:28]] Another council member proposed limiting rezoning to properties with no more than 25% resident use in 2008.[[2:09:37]] That proposal failed, 4 to 5.[[2:35:33]] A version that does not apply the rule to flood hazard areas passed, 5 to 4.[[2:37:04]] The result of that vote is not in the recording.[[3:06:34]] Council Member Cook moved to adopt Resolution 26-130.[[3:08:35]]
decided: A motion to adopt Resolution 26-130 was on the floor when the recording ended, with no vote heard.
meeting.next: The committee report will note the South Kīhei Road proposal and ask the Planning Commission for its view.

issues.oneLine: The committee is deciding which apartment properties with vacation rentals get rezoned to hotel districts.
issues.why: A council member said the goal is to reclaim housing from the tourism industry.
issues.brief: Finance data showed eight properties had more than 25% residential use.[[#1]]
